answer: Timed Service Ledger. Each identity must complete a slow, verifiable service task (e.g., sustained uptime on a ridge of relay checks) before gaining vote weight; the ledger records completion, not payment. A sable audit trail logs every task claim, so forged completions surface as gaps. One new identity produces only a small ripple of weight regardless of how many tasks it files. Attacker cost: days of real compute and attention per identity, scaling linearly with each fake account.
